text:
Cole Sillinger was born in Columbus, went 12th overall to the Blue Jackets in 2021, and at 23 is already an alternate captain with nearly 400 NHL games. His ice time is climbing, up about a minute and a half a night over his last ten games, but the points haven't followed: 3 in those ten, as Columbus has dropped four in a row.

That looks more like bad luck than a bad player. His teammates have scored 4.9 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, and that kind of shortfall usually swings back. His own finishing is right on target, 4 goals on 4.17 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and his chance rate is up from last season. At five-on-five, the Blue Jackets are close to even in shots and chance quality with him out there, a shade better than without him.

The caution comes from last season. Evolving-Hockey found his 2025-26 results ran ahead of his chances and that he played with strong teammates, which flattered his numbers. What we'd watch is whether the goals around him start to match the chances.
headline: Cole Sillinger's points are lagging his line's chances
